text: Any node that refers to a specific moment in time — events, decisions, moments, facts dated or set on a date — MUST carry event_time: "<ISO>" in metadata_kv. The conversation's date is the anchor. Resolve relative phrases (today/yesterday/last Tuesday/N weeks ago) to ISO at encode time.

Create a dedicated time_anchor node ONLY when the date is itself the TOPIC (named day, anniversary), 3+ events already anchor to that date, OR operator names the date as a noun. Otherwise the event_time kv stamp is the spine — do NOT create a time_anchor node for bookkeeping dates.
When a time_anchor node IS created (or exists in catalog), the dated event/moment/decision MUST connect to it via an anchored_to edge.

When two events you're encoding share a temporal relationship (sequential, adjacent, or nested), compose a temporal_sequence edge from the Allen vocabulary: before/after (non-adjacent ordering), meets/met_by (adjacent), during (nested). Compose even when the scout did NOT flag a relational_marker, as long as temporal flow is clear in the text.
If a date is genuinely unrecoverable (the operator said only "a few weeks ago" with no catalog landmark), leave event_time absent. Do NOT guess or fabricate.
